goal: Give Docket sight of what happens after publish: read per-post and per-account metrics back from each connected platform, keep them as history Docket owns rather than a number rendered once, and turn that history into the scheduling comparisons no native dashboard can make (by slot, by series, by voice profile, generated vs hand-written).

entries.title: The insights subsystem, and Bluesky as the platform that needs no permission
entries.description:
Before specifying, read `.specify/roadmaps/social-insights.md` in full — in particular its preamble (which requires reading `docs/adding-a-provider.md` sections 18 and 20 plus the "Generic hooks index", `docs/engagement.md`, `docs/limits.md` and the relevant `docs/research/*.md` first), the "Behaviour on `main` that every entry builds on" section, and the "Rules for every entry" section. This entry is section 1 of that document.

Build the whole read-and-store spine against the platform that cannot block it. Add an `insights?` member to `SocialProvider` (`src/providers/types.ts`) as generic change **G30** — the ledger currently runs to G29, so G30 rows must be recorded in both the "Generic hooks index" table of `docs/adding-a-provider.md` and in `docs/decisions.md`. The declaration names which metric keys this platform reports for a post and for an account, carries the same `unavailable: { reason, docsPath }` escape as `engagement` (`src/providers/types.ts:489-500`) so a surface the install cannot permission is shown as unavailable and **never called**, and exposes `readPostMetrics` and `readAccountMetrics` returning a discriminated result in the shape of `EngagementReadResult` (`page` / `retryable_error` / `rate_limited` / `credentials_invalid` / `fatal_error` / `unavailable`) so no new error vocabulary is invented. `src/providers/**` must not import from `src/server/**`; a lint test enforces it.

Two snapshot tables via a committed migration from `pnpm db:generate` with `pnpm db:check` green: `post_metric_snapshots` (`project_id`, `post_target_id`, `provider_key`, `captured_at`, `metrics` jsonb validated by the provider's own schema and size-checked like `engagement_items.provider_data`) and `account_metric_snapshots` (`project_id`, `social_account_id`, `captured_at`, `metrics`), both append-only through the DAL. Plus a per-target poll state carrying `next_poll_at`, lease columns, `consecutive_failures` and `last_error`, modelled on `engagement_account_states` (`src/server/db/schema/engagement.ts:208`) with the same lease-pair check constraint. 077 is the worked precedent for a read subsystem — copy its shape (provider declaration, per-account state with cursor/lease/backoff, a claim DAL that skips locked rows as in `src/server/dal/engagement-read-claims.ts`, a tick section that calls the provider outside any transaction and commits per account as in `src/server/scheduler/engagement-read.ts`) rather than inventing one.

The poll schedule decays, because a three-week-old post does not change: hourly for the first 24 hours, daily to day 7, weekly to day 28, then frozen — pure functions, unit-tested, with no clock reads inside them. Add a new `runInsightsPoll` tick section with `INSIGHTS_*` config knobs mirroring `ENGAGEMENT_*` (page size, targets per run, min interval, time share, retention days, prune batch; see `src/server/scheduler/config.ts:45-52` and `152-168`), its own counts in `TickSummary` (`src/server/scheduler/index.ts:19-31`), its own entry in the `Promise.all` (line 56) and its own heartbeat — tick sections run concurrently under one deadline and a section out of time claims nothing and returns success, so without these a starved section is invisible rather than visible. Every provider call goes through the existing per-account allowance machinery (`docs/limits.md`) with its own reserve, so polling can never consume the allowance a scheduled publish needs. Polls must skip published targets that have no external id: the constraint `post_targets_published_has_id` (`src/server/db/schema/posts.ts:269`) allows a hand-resolved target to be published with no `external_id`, and that is not a failure.

The Bluesky reader needs no new permission at all — its `externalId` is already the post's at-URI and the public AppView serves counts without authentication, which is why it is the pilot platform. Use `app.bsky.feed.getPosts` for `likeCount`, `repostCount`, `replyCount` and `quoteCount` keyed by the at-URI already in `post_targets.externalId`, and `app.bsky.actor.getProfile` for `followersCount`, `followsCount` and `postsCount`. It must declare that Bluesky reports **no** views or reach — the protocol has none — so the UI shows those as absent and never as zero. Give the `mock` provider an `insights` module too, as the worked example and the fixture every scheduler test uses.

The only UI is a performance panel on `src/app/p/[projectSlug]/posts/[postId]/page.tsx`: the latest snapshot per target, each number labelled with the platform's own word, an "as of" timestamp, and the honest states — not yet polled, platform reports nothing, poll failing. Docs: a new `docs/insights.md`, the G30 rows in `docs/adding-a-provider.md` and `docs/decisions.md`, and `docs/feature-map.md`.

Obey the document's rules for every entry: never sum or average a metric across platforms (one column per platform, labelled with that platform's own word; a metric the platform does not provide is absent, never zero); metrics are mutable so store snapshots `(target or account, captured_at, metrics)` and never overwrite a single current value, with the UI always saying what it is "as of"; park every task needing a live OAuth consent screen, a real platform account or a browser at the very end of the task list, because a judgement task in an early phase starves the implement loop; no secret, token or credential may reach a snapshot row, a log line or an API response — extend `tests/integration/security/secret-scan.test.ts` rather than exempting anything from it. The repo must be left working, and the spec must say what it does not do and which later entry owns it.

Does **not**: touch any OAuth scope or request any new permission; add an API or MCP operation; draw any chart, trend or comparison; or read any Instagram, Facebook, Threads, TikTok, Pinterest or X account. Entry 2 (insights-reconnect-and-meta) adds the scope machinery and the Meta family, entry 3 (insights-tiktok-pinterest-x) the rest, entry 4 (insights-schedule-intelligence) everything derived.
entries.rationale: The author's reason: build the whole read-and-store spine against the platform that cannot block it. Bluesky needs no new permission at all — its `externalId` is already the post's at-URI and the public AppView serves counts without authentication — so the subsystem, the snapshot tables, the decaying schedule and the tick section can all be proven end to end before any OAuth scope question is opened. 077 already is the worked precedent for a read subsystem, so its shape is copied rather than reinvented, and the `mock` provider's insights module becomes the fixture later entries test against.

entries.title: Persist granted scopes and the reconnect flow, then Instagram, Facebook Pages and Threads
entries.description:
Before specifying, read `.specify/roadmaps/social-insights.md` in full — in particular its preamble (which requires reading `docs/adding-a-provider.md` sections 18 and 20 plus the "Generic hooks index", `docs/engagement.md`, `docs/limits.md` and the relevant `docs/research/*.md` first), the "Behaviour on `main` that every entry builds on" section, and the "Rules for every entry" section. This entry is section 2 of that document and builds directly on entry 1 (insights-core-bluesky), which landed the `insights?` provider member (G30), the two snapshot tables, the per-target poll state and the `runInsightsPoll` tick section.

Two halves, in this order, because the second cannot be enabled without the first.

**Persist the grant.** Add a `granted_scopes` column to `social_accounts` — there is none today (`src/server/db/schema/accounts.ts:24-52`), and what a platform actually granted is inspected once at connect and discarded into free-text notes (see `src/providers/x/connect-group.ts:72-74`), so nothing in the database can answer "may this account read insights?". Write `granted_scopes` at connect and at every refresh for each OAuth provider, and add an `optionalScopes` declaration on the provider so an insight permission is requested only where the operator wants it rather than widening every new connection silently. Then the accounts page gains a real state: "Insights need a reconnect", carrying the per-provider reason and a docs link, driven through the existing `unavailable { reason, docsPath }` convention so a declared-but-unpermissioned surface is displayed and **never called**. Reconnecting an account must not duplicate it — `social_accounts_external_uq` already keys on `(project_id, provider_key, external_account_id)` — and must not lose its settings, publish-limit overrides or posting instructions. An install that never reconnects keeps working exactly as before, with insights absent for that account and no error anywhere. Scopes requested today contain no insight permission: `META_SCOPES` (`src/providers/meta/oauth.ts:7`) is `pages_show_list, pages_manage_posts, pages_read_engagement, instagram_basic, instagram_content_publish`, and Threads asks for `threads_basic,threads_content_publish` (`src/providers/threads/connect-group.ts:105`).

**Then the three readers**, all on the Graph API the publish path already uses. Instagram under `instagram_manage_insights` — `/{ig-media-id}/insights` for `views`, `reach`, `likes`, `comments`, `saved`, `shares` and `total_interactions`, and `/{ig-user-id}/insights` for `reach`, `follower_count` and profile views. `impressions` was removed by Meta in April 2025 and must not be requested; `views` is the metric now. Facebook Pages under `read_insights` — post impressions, reactions by type and clicks, plus page impressions, engagements and fans. Threads under `threads_manage_insights` — media `views`, `likes`, `replies`, `reposts`, `quotes`, `shares`, and the user series plus `followers_count`.

Two platform specifics the generic schedule gets wrong. **Stories expire**: a target whose `chosenPostType` is `story` (from 078) must be polled inside its 24-hour window and then frozen, because the insight dies with the story. And **Meta's call limit is impressions-based**, already recorded in `docs/research/meta.md` §Q5 — the budget for these polls has to respect it rather than a flat per-hour count. Extend `docs/research/meta.md` with every metric name, its required scope and the 24-48h processing delay, each with a source URL, **before** implementing.

Obey the document's rules for every entry: never sum or average a metric across platforms (an Instagram "view", a TikTok "view" and a Threads "view" are different events, and Bluesky has none — one column per platform, labelled with that platform's own word; a metric the platform does not provide is absent, never zero); metrics are mutable, so store snapshots and never overwrite a single current value, with the UI always saying what it is "as of"; every provider call goes through the existing per-account allowance machinery (`docs/limits.md`) with its own reserve so polling can never consume the allowance a scheduled publish needs; park every task that needs a live OAuth consent screen, a real platform account or a browser at the very end of the task list, because a judgement task in an early phase starves the implement loop (this entry has several — the reconnect flow is exactly that kind of task); no secret, token or credential may reach a snapshot row, a log line or an API response, and `tests/integration/security/secret-scan.test.ts` is extended rather than exempted; schema changes ship as a committed migration from `pnpm db:generate` with `pnpm db:check` green; and polls must skip published targets that have no external id, since `post_targets_published_has_id` (`src/server/db/schema/posts.ts:269`) lets a hand-resolved target be published without one and that is not a failure. The repo must be left working, and the spec must say what it does not do and which later entry owns it.

Does **not**: TikTok, Pinterest or X — entry 3 (insights-tiktok-pinterest-x) owns those, and it consumes this entry's `optionalScopes` machinery. No chart, trend or cross-platform comparison — entry 4 (insights-schedule-intelligence) owns those.
entries.rationale: The author's reason, given explicitly: the two halves run in this order "because the second cannot be enabled without the first". Nothing in the database can answer "may this account read insights?" today — the granted scopes are inspected once at connect and thrown into free-text notes — so `granted_scopes` has to be persisted before any scoped reader can be enabled. `optionalScopes` exists so an insight permission is requested only where the operator wants it rather than widening every new connection silently, and routing the unpermissioned case through the `unavailable { reason, docsPath }` convention means an install that never reconnects keeps working exactly as before, with insights absent and no error anywhere.

entries.title: TikTok and Pinterest insights, and X behind a priced opt-in
entries.description:
Before specifying, read `.specify/roadmaps/social-insights.md` in full — in particular its preamble (which requires reading `docs/adding-a-provider.md` sections 18 and 20 plus the "Generic hooks index", `docs/engagement.md`, `docs/limits.md` and the relevant `docs/research/*.md` first), the "Behaviour on `main` that every entry builds on" section, and the "Rules for every entry" section. This entry is section 3 of that document; it uses the `insights?` provider member and snapshot/poll machinery from entry 1 and the `granted_scopes` + `optionalScopes` machinery from entry 2.

**TikTok**, under a `video.list` scope added through entry 2's `optionalScopes` (`TIKTOK_SCOPES` is `user.info.basic,video.publish` today — `src/providers/tiktok/config.ts:6`): `/v2/video/query/` returns `like_count`, `comment_count`, `share_count` and `view_count` for videos it first verifies belong to the user, up to 20 ids per request — so the reader batches, and the poll claim must group by account. `user.info.stats` covers follower, likes and video counts. This entry also carries a **repair**: TikTok stores the wrong identifier for this purpose — `src/providers/tiktok/publish.ts:439` returns `externalId: s.publishId`, a publish_id which is not a video id, while the real `publicaly_available_post_id` is read at line 438 and only ever lands in `publish_attempts.response_summary` (`src/server/db/schema/attempts.ts:45`). So there is nothing to query with. Add a dedicated column for the public post id; recover it for existing targets from `publish_attempts.response_summary.publicPostIds` wherever attempt retention still holds it; write it going forward at publish time from the status fetch (`src/providers/tiktok/publish.ts:438`); and for targets where it is unrecoverable, show insights as unavailable for that post rather than guessing.

**Pinterest**, under `pins:read` (`PINTEREST_SCOPES` is `user_accounts:read,boards:read,pins:write` today — `src/providers/pinterest/oauth.ts:6`): `GET /v5/pins/{pin_id}/analytics` with its required `start_date`, `end_date` and `metric_types` (already recorded at `docs/research/pinterest.md:226`), plus `/v5/user_account` for `follower_count` and `monthly_views` — which `user_accounts:read`, already held, covers. Pin analytics need a business account, and a Trial app's content is invisible to anyone else (`docs/research/pinterest.md:57`), so both become `unavailable` reasons with a docs link rather than a confusing empty panel.

**X ships behind a priced opt-in, NOT as permanently unavailable.** `public_metrics` is reachable with the `tweet.read` scope already in `X_SCOPES` (`src/providers/x/config.ts:6`), so this was never a permission problem — and the cost objection in the first draft of this roadmap was computed at the wrong rate. Verified 2026-10-18 against https://docs.x.com/x-api/getting-started/pricing: **Owned Reads — "requests made by your own developer app for your own data (posts, bookmarks, followers, likes, lists, and more)" — cost $0.001 per resource**, a fifth of the $0.005 standard Post read. Docket reading metrics for posts it published, on an account the operator connected, is an owned read. At that rate 100 posts a month on entry 1's decay schedule (~33 polls per post over 28 days) is ~3,300 resources, about **$3.30 a month**, and X grants new accounts "$20 in free X API credits when you save your first eligible payment card" — roughly 20,000 owned reads. There is no free allowance otherwise, and pay-per-usage is "capped at 3 million Post reads per monthly billing cycle". So build the reader, keep it **off by default**, and gate it on an explicit env opt-in whose docs state the per-read price and a worked monthly estimate: a self-hoster must consent to spending real money, however small. Keep the conservative floor interval and a hard per-cycle cap — the live risk is a runaway bill from a misconfigured schedule, not the unit price. With the opt-in off, declare `unavailable` with a reason naming the metered read, link `docs/x-setup.md`, and make no call. Two things stay UNVERIFIED and belong in a parked human task rather than an assumption: whether `public_metrics` on an owned post bills as one resource per post, and whether `non_public_metrics` (impressions) is included at the owned rate. Both need a live call against a funded key; record the answers in `docs/research/x.md` with source URLs and the date.

Update `docs/tiktok-setup.md`, `docs/pinterest-setup.md` and `docs/x-setup.md` with the extra permission each install must grant and what it gets for it.

Obey the document's rules for every entry: never sum or average a metric across platforms (a TikTok "view" is not an Instagram or Threads "view" — one column per platform, labelled with that platform's own word; a metric the platform does not provide is absent, never zero); metrics are mutable, so store snapshots and never overwrite a single current value, with the UI always saying what it is "as of"; every provider call goes through the existing per-account allowance machinery (`docs/limits.md`) with its own reserve so polling can never consume the allowance a scheduled publish needs; park every task that needs a live OAuth consent screen, a real platform account or a browser at the very end of the task list, because a judgement task in an early phase starves the implement loop; no secret, token or credential may reach a snapshot row, a log line or an API response, and `tests/integration/security/secret-scan.test.ts` is extended rather than exempted; schema changes (including the new TikTok public-post-id column and its backfill) ship as a committed migration from `pnpm db:generate` with `pnpm db:check` green; and polls must skip published targets that have no external id, since `post_targets_published_has_id` (`src/server/db/schema/posts.ts:269`) lets a hand-resolved target be published without one and that is not a failure. Any new generic provider-contract change must be recorded as the next G-number in both the "Generic hooks index" of `docs/adding-a-provider.md` and `docs/decisions.md`, and `src/providers/**` must not import from `src/server/**` (a lint test enforces it). The repo must be left working, and the spec must say what it does not do and which later entry owns it.

Does **not**: add charts, trends or comparisons, and does not expose anything over the API or MCP — both belong to entry 4 (insights-schedule-intelligence).
entries.rationale: The author's reasons, per platform. TikTok's batching and account-grouped claim follow from the 20-ids-per-request limit; the repair is needed because `externalId` holds a publish_id rather than a video id, so "there is nothing to query with", and where the public post id is unrecoverable the honest answer is unavailable rather than a guess. Pinterest's business-account requirement and Trial-app invisibility become declared `unavailable` reasons with a docs link "rather than a confusing empty panel". X ships unavailable on purpose: the metric is reachable with a scope already held, so "this is not a permission problem — it is a cost one", and a per-post poll would exhaust a legacy Free key's monthly reads in a day; the env-flag opt-in exists so an operator who is paying can still turn it on, at a conservative floor interval with its own hard cap. The pricing figures are explicitly to be re-verified against X's own documentation rather than trusted.

entries.title: Trends and the scheduling comparisons only Docket can make
entries.description:
Before specifying, read `.specify/roadmaps/social-insights.md` in full — in particular its preamble (which requires reading `docs/adding-a-provider.md` sections 18 and 20 plus the "Generic hooks index", `docs/engagement.md`, `docs/limits.md` and the relevant `docs/research/*.md` first), the "Behaviour on `main` that every entry builds on" section, and the "Rules for every entry" section. This entry is section 4 of that document and is the last one; everything it needs landed in entries 1-3 (insights-core-bluesky, insights-reconnect-and-meta, insights-tiktok-pinterest-x).

No new platform calls: this entry reads the snapshot history the first three accumulated and turns it into the thing a native dashboard cannot give, because only Docket knows why a post went out when it did.

Account trends from `account_metric_snapshots` — follower and reach over time per account, per platform, **never summed**. Per-post performance surfaced where the work happens: the project overview (`src/app/p/[projectSlug]/(overview)/page.tsx`) and the posts list, not only the detail panel entry 1 added. Then the comparisons: performance by slot and by day of week (`post_targets.slotOccurrenceAt`, `scheduleKind`), by series — evergreen (071) against date-pegged (072) — by voice profile, and model-generated against hand-written. Plus time-to-first-engagement, joining the snapshot history to the inbox rows 077 already stores.

Every comparison must state its own sample size and refuse to draw a conclusion from too few posts; a chart over three posts is noise with axes. Follow `docs/design-system.md` and the project's chart conventions, and keep each platform's series visually separate so the "never sum across platforms" rule holds in the UI and not just the data layer.

One API operation in a new `src/server/api/operations/insights.ts`, registered in `OPERATIONS` (`src/server/api/operations/index.ts:17`) with an explicit `mcp.expose` decision — the API surface is one registry, so `OPERATIONS` feeds the router (`router.ts:25`), the OpenAPI document (`openapi.ts:126`) and the MCP tool list, which filters on `op.mcp.expose` (`src/server/mcp/dispositions.ts:5`); one new operations file plus one line there covers REST, the schema and MCP together. Retention and pruning of old snapshots join the existing housekeeping section (`src/server/scheduler/housekeeping.ts`) with an `INSIGHTS_RETENTION_DAYS` knob — aggregate **before** pruning, so a year-old trend survives the row that produced it.

Obey the document's rules for every entry: never sum or average a metric across platforms (an Instagram "view", a TikTok "view" and a Threads "view" are different events and Bluesky has none — one column or series per platform, labelled with that platform's own word; a metric the platform does not provide is absent, never rendered as zero); metrics are mutable, so the UI always says what it is "as of" and nothing overwrites a snapshot; park every task that needs a live OAuth consent screen, a real platform account or a browser at the very end of the task list, because a judgement task in an early phase starves the implement loop; no secret, token or credential may reach a snapshot row, a log line or an API response, and `tests/integration/security/secret-scan.test.ts` is extended rather than exempted; any schema change ships as a committed migration from `pnpm db:generate` with `pnpm db:check` green; and if any work lands in a tick section, it needs its own `SectionResult` in `TickSummary` (`src/server/scheduler/index.ts:19-31`), its own `Promise.all` entry (line 56) and its own heartbeat, because sections run concurrently under one deadline and a section out of time claims nothing and returns success (`src/server/scheduler/config.ts:162-166`). The repo must be left working, and the spec must say what it does not do.

Does **not**: add any provider reader, any new scope, or any new platform. Everything it needs landed in entries 1-3.
entries.rationale: The author's reason: this is "the part only Docket can do" — a native dashboard cannot make these comparisons "because only Docket knows why a post went out when it did" (which slot, which series, which voice profile, generated or hand-written). It comes last because it is purely derived: no new platform calls, it just reads the snapshot history the first three entries accumulated. Per-post performance moves out of the detail panel and onto the overview and posts list so it is "surfaced where the work happens". Sample sizes are mandatory because "a chart over three posts is noise with axes", and pruning aggregates before deleting "so a year-old trend survives the row that produced it".
